title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: edit ServiceNow user mapping and query filters on a published connection
summary: The briefing passes: the connection-editing capability, licensing statements and roadmap dates are supported. It correctly reports Microsoft's conflicting mapping and query-edit documentation, but should also flag the conflicting instruction about excluding already indexed content and align its checklist with its controls table.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can edit a published ServiceNow connector's user mapping without recreating the connection.
claims.quote: Previously, once the ServiceNow connector was configured, user mappings and query filters could not be changed without recreating the connection. Now, admins can edit these settings directly within the connector configuration.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Changing the query filter can narrow what a ServiceNow connection indexes without rebuilding it.
claims.quote: You can modify this filter to index only specific articles based on your organizational needs.
claims.fix: Add after the narrowing-filter advice: 'The manage page also says that excluding items already indexed requires deleting the existing connection and creating a new one with a data source exclusion filter; this conflicts with its edit-support table.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/manage-connector.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A query string determines which ServiceNow articles are selected for indexing, so widening its scope can select more content.
claims.quote: ServiceNow uses the following default filter: active=true^workflow_state=published. You can modify this filter to index only specific articles based on your organizational needs.

claims.claim: The Everyone access-permissions choice shows indexed data in search results for all users.
claims.quote: If you choose Everyone, indexed data appears in the search results for all users.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation operation that edits these ServiceNow connection query filters, advanced criteria and user mappings.
claims.quote: Searched: ServiceNow connector edit query string user mapping Microsoft Graph beta API PowerShell; ServiceNow user mapping query API externalConnection. Read v1.0 and beta externalConnection update references and beta configuration resource; none exposes these ServiceNow settings.

claims.claim: The Graph externalConnection update reference lists configuration as an updatable property.
claims.quote: configuration | microsoft.graph.externalConnectors.configuration | Specifies additional application IDs that are allowed to manage the connection and to index content in the connection.

claims.claim: The Graph externalConnection update reference lists description as an updatable property.
claims.quote: description | String | Description of the connection displayed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Graph externalConnection update reference lists name as an updatable property.
claims.quote: name | String | The display name of the connection to be displayed in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Maximum length of 128 characters.

claims.claim: The Graph externalConnection update reference provides no route to the ServiceNow user mapping.
claims.quote: Searched: ServiceNow connector edit query string user mapping Microsoft Graph beta API PowerShell. Read externalConnection update v1.0 and beta and configuration beta: only configuration, description and name are updatable; configuration contains authorizedAppIds, not user mappings.

claims.claim: The Graph externalConnection update reference provides no route to the ServiceNow query string.
claims.quote: Searched: ServiceNow user mapping query API externalConnection. Read externalConnection update v1.0 and beta and configuration beta: only configuration, description and name are updatable; configuration contains authorizedAppIds, not query strings.

claims.claim: The identity-mapping page does not support conditional mappings.
claims.quote: Only one mapping is supported for all users. Conditional mappings aren't supported.
